**What we’re adding** A *referral code* that anyone can share. When a new user signs up with that code, they (the new user) automatically receive a £10 credit that can be applied to their first purchase. The person who generated the code gets **no active benefit**—just the ability to create and share codes. **Why we need safety steps** | Feature | Safety parts we’ll build | |---------|--------------------------| | Referrals with credits | • Store each code in a table that only the creator can edit or delete.
• Limit each code to one use per invited user.
• Keep the £10 credit in a “balance” column that the server can modify only for that user.
• Log the credit grant on the server so we can audit it.
• No shareable secret keys in the client code – the code is just a small random string. | | Stripe usage | • Credit will **never** be passed directly to Stripe; it will just reduce the amount charged on checkout.
• Rate‑limit how many credits a single account can grant per month (e.g. 5 codes). | | Logins | • Only signed‑in users can create a code; we’ll use Supabase Auth’s built‑in magic‑link. | | Data privacy | • Each user sees only their own referral codes and balance. | --- ## Starter questions (Amber level) 1. **How many credits per user?** *e.g. “A user can create up to 5 unique referral codes per month.”* 2. **Do you want a page for users to see and copy their code?** If yes, we’ll make a simple “My Referrals” page. 3. **When do the credits apply?** - Immediately after the invitee signs up **and** before they first checkout? - Or only once the invited user makes their first purchase? 4. **What happens if someone signs up with an invalid or already‑used code?** We’ll show a friendly error and allow “no credit.” Feel free to answer with the default or any tweaks. Once you give a quick answer, I’ll create a concise plan (one‑screen) and we’ll walk through each step. --- ### One‑screen plan (draft) ``` What we are building: A “Referral Code” feature that gives a £10 credit to new users who sign up using a code shared by a friend. Who uses it: Anyone signing up through the website. Risk level: Amber (logins, Stripe, credits). Day‑one features: 1. A table `referral_codes` (creator_id, code, uses, created_at). 2. A UI page "My Referrals" where logged‑in users can see their codes and copy them. 3. Backend API that validates a code on signup, grants a £10 credit (balance, maybe a db column), and ensures one‑time use per invitee. 4. Stripe checkout integration that subtracts the credit from the first charge. Information it stores: - Referral codes (public code string, creator id, usage count). - User balances (private; each user sees only their own). - Sign‑up logs for audit. Logins: Supabase Auth (magic link). Payments: Stripe Checkout for purchases; credit is applied server‑side. RLS policies: `referral_codes` & `balances` tables set to RLS, only the creator or the credited user can modify them. Building steps (one at a time, with proof each step): 1. Create the `referral_codes` table + RLS. 2. Add a next-auth‑style “My Referrals” page. 3. Create a serverless function `/api/validate-referral` that checks the code and records a credit on the user’s balance. 4. Update signup flow to send a code param to that function. 5. Update Stripe checkout to read the balance and subtract it. 6. Add tests / manual checks.
